_README: Industry events / semiconductor conferences that can move watchlist names via product announcements, roadmap disclosures, or competitive read-through. The morning routine (CLAUDE.md) refreshes dates and 'watch' notes via web search each run and adds newly-announced events. 'tickers' = watchlist symbols with direct or read-through exposure. 'partners' = KEY PRIVATE/NON-WATCHLIST COMPANIES whose appearances matter because a holding depends on them (e.g. Ayar Labs is Sivers' flagship CPO customer; Lightmatter is the CPO peer benchmark). ADDED 2026-08-07 after OCP APAC was missed: relevance must be checked against BOTH tickers and partners, and MAJOR EVENT SERIES HAVE REGIONAL EDITIONS (OCP runs Global + APAC + EMEA; SEMICON runs West/Taiwan/Europe/Korea) — enumerate every edition, not just the flagship. 'confidence': confirmed (dates verified) | approx (typical timing, verify) | rumored. Dates ISO YYYY-MM-DD, event-local. Not investment advice.

events.name: Hot Interconnects 2026 (33rd IEEE Symposium on High-Performance Interconnects)
events.watch: ADDED 2026-08-14 (morning run) — a real calendar gap, found while verifying the Hot Chips keynote roster. The 33rd IEEE Symposium on High-Performance Interconnects (HotI) runs **Aug 19-21, 2026, virtual**, theme **'Scale-Up, Scale-Out, Scale-Across: Do they really differ?'** It sits in the two-day gap between Rosenblatt (Aug 17-18) and Hot Chips (Aug 23-25) and had been missed on every prior pass. **How it entered the file matters: a search result attributed NVIDIA's Gilad Shainer keynote 'Networking Innovations for Gigascale AI Systems' to Hot Chips; NVIDIA's own event page places it at Hot Interconnects instead — so the Hot Chips second keynote remains unnamed (nineteenth consecutive pass) and this event exists.** **Direct watchlist exposure is via the sponsor and speaker roster, not read-through: Marvell is a Diamond sponsor alongside Lightmatter and Napatech; Broadcom and Meta are Platinum sponsors alongside Qualcomm, Cisco and Eliyan; NVIDIA supplies the networking keynote (Shainer, SVP Networking).** **The reason this entry earns its place in an optics book is Lightmatter — the CPO peer benchmark named in 'partners' — presenting twice on the opening morning: Nick Harris (Founder/CEO) at 10:15am on 'BiDi DWDM: The Interconnect Foundation for High-Performance AI Training and Inference', and Arul Madhavan (Sr Staff ML Engineer) at 10:40am on 'Scaling Inference Prefill with High-Radix Photonic Interconnect' (Passage/Guide product lines).** That is the competitive field around SIVE and SOI stating its own scale-up architecture case on the record, four days before SPIE and five weeks before ECOC. Avicena is also present Aug 19-21. **Calibrate it correctly: HotI is an academic/technical symposium with a papers track, not a product venue and not a sell-side event — it produces architecture disclosure and direction, not guidance or orders.** Its value here is sequencing: Lightmatter's scale-up photonics case (Aug 19) lands BEFORE NVIDIA's Vera/Rubin/BlueField-4/Spectrum-X disclosures at Hot Chips (Aug 23-25), which in turn land one day before NVDA's Q2 FY2027 print (Aug 26), with MRVL Aug 27 and AVGO Sep 2. No keynote list beyond Shainer was published at source as of this pass. **Nothing here adjudicates any SIVE or SOI falsifier** — treat as competitive-field intelligence. 5 days out. **Re-checked 2026-08-14 (end-of-day run) — no program change since the morning pass; stamp only.** Gilad Shainer (NVIDIA SVP Networking) keynote and Lightmatter's two opening-morning talks (Harris 10:15am on BiDi DWDM, Madhavan 10:40am on high-radix photonic interconnect) all unchanged at source, Avicena still present, no additional keynotes published. The sequencing point is what tightened: HotI now opens in 5 days and the chain behind it is intact — Lightmatter's scale-up photonics case (Aug 19) → NVIDIA's Vera/Rubin/BlueField-4/Spectrum-X disclosures at Hot Chips (Aug 23-25) → NVDA's Q2 FY2027 print (Aug 26) → MRVL (Aug 27) → AVGO (Sep 2). **Nothing here adjudicates any SIVE or SOI falsifier** — competitive-field intelligence only. 5 days out. **Re-verified 2026-08-17 end-of-day run at source (hoti.org/2026) — dates confirmed Aug 19-21, virtual, theme unchanged ('Scale-Up, Scale-Out, Scale-Across: Do they really differ?'). This pass found REAL new program content: the keynote slate has gone from one name to three.** **Newly named: Omar Baldonado (Senior Director, Meta) — 'Lessons from networking Meta's gigawatt-scale AI fleet' — and Bilal Riaz (Ciena) — 'The Future of AI Interconnects: Open Approaches to High-Performance AI Infrastructure'**, joining the previously-logged **Gilad Shainer (NVIDIA)** on 'Networking Innovations for Gigascale AI Systems'. Note one attribution correction: the source page lists Shainer as **SVP Marketing**, not SVP Networking as this entry previously recorded. **The Meta keynote is the addition that matters for this book.** Meta is a watchlist name already on this entry, and an operator talking about what actually broke at gigawatt scale is a different class of evidence from a vendor talking about what it sells — it is the demand side describing its own constraints, which is the scarcest input in the optics chain. **Also new at source: a Meta lightning session by Drew Alduino on the OCI MSA (Optical Compute Interface)** — a multi-source standards effort for optical interconnect, i.e. the hyperscaler pushing to commoditise the layer that SIVE and SOI sit upstream of. That cuts both ways for the optics thesis (volume up, differentiation down) and is worth watching rather than scoring. Sponsor tiers re-confirmed unchanged: **Marvell, Lightmatter and Napatech Diamond; Qualcomm, Cisco, Broadcom, Meta and Eliyan Platinum.** Lightmatter's two opening-morning talks (Nick Harris 10:15am on BiDi DWDM; Arul Madhavan 10:40am on high-radix photonic interconnect) were not individually re-listed on the page read this pass and are carried forward from the 08-14 verification rather than re-confirmed. Calibration unchanged: HotI is an academic/technical symposium with a papers track — architecture disclosure and direction, not guidance or orders. **Nothing here adjudicates any SIVE or SOI falsifier**; competitive-field intelligence only. The sequencing chain is intact and tightening: Lightmatter's scale-up photonics case (Aug 19) → NVIDIA's Vera/Rubin/BlueField-4/Spectrum-X disclosures at Hot Chips (Aug 23-25) → NVDA's Q2 FY2027 print (Aug 26) → MRVL (Aug 27) → AVGO (Sep 2). 2 days out — the nearest catalyst on this calendar once Rosenblatt closes tomorrow. **Re-verified 2026-08-18 morning run at source (hoti.org/2026) — dates confirmed Aug 19-21, virtual. Two genuinely new items this pass, and one correction to yesterday's entry.** **(1) The lightning session logged yesterday as "a Meta lightning session by Drew Alduino on the OCI MSA" is bigger than that: the source page shows a lightning session covering FOUR newly-announced Multi-Source Agreements — OCI MSA (Optical Compute Interface), Open CPX MSA, SDM4 MCF MSA and XPO MSA.** That is four separate standards efforts for optical/advanced interconnect being introduced on one stage in a single week. **For an optics book this is the most important thing on the program and it cuts both ways, hard:** MSAs exist to make a layer multi-source and interchangeable, which raises volume and lowers the differentiation premium of any single supplier sitting upstream of it — i.e. the same ambivalence flagged yesterday for OCI alone, now multiplied by four. **SDM4 MCF is worth separating out** — multi-core fibre is a *fibre-side* capacity answer rather than a transceiver-side one, so it is a different competitive axis from CPO entirely. None of this adjudicates a SIVE or SOI falsifier; it is the field defining the interfaces those companies will have to sell into. **(2) The Gold and Silver sponsor tiers resolved this pass and add two consortium names that matter for the same reason: UALink Consortium and UCIe are Gold sponsors, Netpreme is Silver** — scale-up and die-to-die interconnect standards bodies sponsoring the venue where the optical MSAs are being launched. **(3) A panel on edge-datacenter interconnects is also on the program**, not previously logged. The three keynotes are re-confirmed unchanged and complete at source: **Gilad Shainer (NVIDIA, SVP Marketing) 'Networking Innovations for Gigascale AI Systems'; Omar Baldonado (Senior Director of Networking, Meta) 'Lessons from networking Meta's gigawatt-scale AI fleet'; Bilal Riaz (Senior Director of Product Line Management and Head of Interconnect Strategy, Ciena) 'The Future of AI Interconnects: Open Approaches to High-Performance AI Infrastructure'.** Diamond sponsors Lightmatter, Marvell and Napatech and Platinum sponsors Qualcomm, Cisco, Broadcom, Meta and Eliyan are unchanged. Lightmatter's two opening-morning talks (Nick Harris 10:15am on BiDi DWDM; Arul Madhavan 10:40am on high-radix photonic interconnect) were again not individually listed on the page read this pass and remain carried forward from the 08-14 verification rather than re-confirmed — treat them as probable, not certain. Calibration unchanged: an academic/technical symposium, architecture disclosure not guidance. Sequencing chain intact: HotI (Aug 19-21) → Hot Chips (Aug 23-25) → NVDA Q2 FY2027 (Aug 26) → MRVL (Aug 27) → AVGO (Sep 2). **1 day out — the nearest catalyst on this calendar as of tomorrow.**

events.name: SPIE Optics + Photonics 2026
events.watch: Added 2026-08-03: dates verified against SPIE's own listing — conferences Aug 23-27, exhibition Aug 25-27, courses Aug 23-26. Calibrate expectations: this is SPIE's RESEARCH-tier optics meeting (optical engineering, nanophotonics, optoelectronic materials, quantum), NOT the datacom/telecom product venue — ECOC (Sep 20-24) and OFC (Mar 2027) remain the real catalyst windows for CPO, 1.6T transceivers and InP-laser roadmaps. Value here is early technical signal on InP/photonic-substrate materials and packaging that shows up as product 12-24 months later, which matters given the InP substrate shortage now documented in the SIVE file (AXT/Lumentum LTA to 2031, Lumentum CEO citing a >30% demand-supply gap). events.name: Marvell Technology Investor Day 2026
events.location: New York City (in-person by invitation; live webcast)
events.watch: **ADDED 2026-08-18 (morning run) — a real calendar gap: a watchlist company has a confirmed, dated, WEBCAST management event and this calendar did not carry it.** **Marvell announced on 2026-08-03, in the same release that set its Q2 FY2027 earnings call, that it will hold an Investor Day on the morning of Tue Oct 6, 2026 in New York City, with Chairman and CEO Matt Murphy and the senior leadership team presenting.** In-person attendance is by invitation only, but **the event is webcast live via the Events section of investor.marvell.com** — which is what separates this from the broker conferences elsewhere on this calendar: it is a company-controlled disclosure venue with a public feed, not a 1x1 program. It sat unlogged for fifteen days. **Why it matters for this book specifically: an investor day is where multi-year financial targets and segment models get set, and MRVL is the one watchlist name whose thesis turns on a disclosure of exactly that kind.** The MRVL falsifiers are "loss/insourcing of a flagship custom program", "CPO disintermediates pluggable DSPs faster than Marvell adapts", and a shift in data-center guide language — all three are TAM-and-roadmap claims that an investor day either substantiates with a model or conspicuously does not. **Sequencing is the other reason to carry it: the Q2 FY2027 print lands Thu Aug 27 at 1:45pm PT, five and a half weeks BEFORE this event**, so the quarter sets the near-term facts and the investor day sets the multi-year frame on top of them. Note the tape context this is being scheduled into: **UBS cut its MRVL target 340 → 300 on 2026-08-17**, and the name has run 74 → 316 and back inside six months. **Nothing here adjudicates a falsifier yet — it is a scheduled opportunity for one to be adjudicated.** 49 days out; outside the 30-day window, carried so it is not missed again.
